The origin has tangent cone -12(Y²-Z²), so there are five ordinary nodes and source bound excludes others. Coordinates square to (11/560,1/56) and square classes 385=5·7·11 and 14=2·7 are independent. Uniqueness of squared-node pair over the function field plus nondegenerate rational specialization in a normal local ring proves generic independence. Good-reduction spreads finite étale five-node scheme away from finitely many primes; Frobenius in the biquadratic extension gives densities 1/4,3/4 via Chebotarev. Extracted standalone verifier checks all critical exact identities and 18 finite-field examples. Limits: finite examples do not establish infinite density; neither geometric monodromy nor all bad primes asserted.

originality.rationale: The full relevant construction and singularity classification in arXiv:2310.15993v1 (§3.2, §4.2, Proposition 4.2.6) establish the geometric sign quartet, not its rational-function-field splitting field, independence of its two node square classes, or the explicit rational specialization and Frobenius distribution. Follow-up arXiv:2401.00760v1 treats another genus-five Howe model; arXiv:2102.07270v1 treats general sextic construction. Comparison is by implication: sign symmetry by itself gives at most a subgroup of V4 and does not imply full independence or density 1/4. Focused published mathematical-record searches returned unrelated records. Historical unindexed arithmetic computations remain a residual risk.

value.rationale: The source establishes a natural five-node family but only geometric singularities. An exact arithmetic description of the four-node configuration gives the finite field of definition of every node, the generic arithmetic Galois permutation representation, and the complete Frobenius-dependent rational singular-point frequency for a concrete rational curve. The group is not a formality of the published sign symmetry: its maximality requires two nontrivial independent square classes and an exact special fiber. This information is pertinent to arithmetic descent and reduction of singular plane curve models, and is neither a routine restatement nor an arbitrary finite slice.
